name: Philostratus (uncertain which)
bio: The epigram on a painting of Telephus is ascribed to a Philostratus whom Paton’s Index of Authors does not identify further; there were several writers of that name.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 110.

poems.title: Book XVI, 110: On a Picture of Telephus Wounded
poems.author: Philostratus (uncertain which)
poems.text: This, the irresistible chieftain of Teuthrania; this Telephus who once bathed in blood the terrible host of the Greeks when he filled Mysian Caycus to overflowing with slaughter; this, the champion who faced the spear of Peleus, now bearing hidden deep in his thigh a heavy and deadly wound, wastes away as if his life were leaving him, dragging himself along with his living flesh.
